text:
The Kings spoiled Dylan Larkin's Canadiens debut on Monday, winning 2-1 in Montreal after two Habs challenges on Los Angeles goals came up empty, per The Hockey News' Karine Hains. It was a rare night when the result matched the play.

That gap is the story of the season. Los Angeles is 8-12-2 with 50% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and our standings model has it six points behind what its play has earned. The Kings have scored about seven fewer goals than their chances predict and allowed about six more. The top line of Adrian Kempe, Artemi Panarin and Alex Laferriere takes 60% of the expected goals at 5-on-5 and has outscored teams 8-3.

The bad news came the same day. Erik Gustafsson is out two to four weeks with a fractured hand, per Daily Faceoff, and his pair with Brandt Clarke has been the best on the blue line (58% of the chances). Kevin Fiala is back nine months after his Olympic injury, but his line with Mats Zuccarello and Quinton Byfield has only 41% of the chances so far.

Off the ice, Drew Doughty has hired agent Pat Brisson, and Pro Hockey Rumors reports he wants to finish his career with the Kings. Our playoff odds have Los Angeles at 32%. What we'd watch: whether Peter Laviolette's team starts banking the points its chances say it should.
headline: The Kings finally get paid in Montreal
